newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's PAN makes plans for opposition Congress.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's PAN makes plans for opposition Congress.

text.p: Mexico's conservative opposition on Sunday proposed an unprecedented pact on economic and political stability, anticipating that the long-ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI) might lose its majority in Congress in July 6 elections.

In a Guanajuato state convention of the National Action Party (PAN), the party's president, Felipe Calderon Hijojosa, said he would ask President Ernesto Zedillo and other opposition parties to sign the agreement ahead of the crucial vote.

The PRI has controlled the presidency and Congress for 67 straight years, and political analysts are uncertain what might happen if the PRI has an opposition Congress, as some pollsters predict could happen.
Mexicans have never had a modern divided government.
"It's an agreement that we have to make now, precisely so that foreign and national investors make wise economic decisions in favor of the country," Calderon told the party meeting.
Despite the PRI's historic strength at the ballot box, the ruling party has been losing ground to the PAN and the leftist Party of the Democratic Revolution (PRD) in recent local elections.

"We're talking about an accord that goes beyond the mere electoral or political so that a Chamber of Deputies (Congress), in the hands of a party or parties other than that of the president can be an opportunity for a positive transformation," Calderon said.

He also said the agreement was necessary because, he claimed, the PRI was running a sneaky campaign to win the "vote of fear" by telling the citizenry that an opposition Congress would cause "capital flight and chaos."
